api_under_test: registerJob() + a queue driver (createQueueManager / SyncDriver / MemoryDriver, or guren add queue)
Mail subclass (mailable) with build(): to/subject/text, or mail(manager).to().subject().send()
createMailManager + setMailManager / container 'mail' binding (or guren add mail)
harness_signal: The app has no queue or mail wiring at all — the whole subsystem must be brought up. `guren add queue` / `guren add mail` scaffold the providers, sample job and mailable and wire them into src/app.ts in one step; `guren make:job` / `guren make:mail` produce the class shells; `guren context` lists Job.dispatch, Mail, MailManager and the queue drivers. Two traps for the unaided: `Job.dispatch()` throws 'Queue driver not configured' until a driver is set globally (the QueueManager only publishes its default driver once `driver()` is resolved), and `Job.make()` throws 'Container not initialized' because nothing calls setContainer() — the mailer has to be reached via setMailManager()/getMailManager() or captured in the provider. A bare agent may instead fire the mail with setTimeout/queueMicrotask and a hand-rolled console 'transport', which the hidden suite rejects (nothing waits in the queue; nothing passes through the mailer).
